BMBlackKnight_BLXKNTDove.overview:
The Black Knight was introduced in 2578 by Kong Interstellar Corporation as both a front-line combatant and a company- and battalion-level command BattleMech for the Star League Defense Force. Equipped with an advanced communications suite capable of coordinating an entire company of 'Mechs, linking command frequencies across a regiment, and connecting with orbital support satellites, the Black Knight quickly established itself as one of the premier heavy BattleMechs of the Star League era. Built with heavy armor and an all-energy weapons array, the design earned a fearsome reputation that endured across centuries of warfare.

Though the Succession Wars drastically reduced the Black Knight's numbers, the design survived through ComStar stockpiles, field modifications, and the determination of its operators. Production eventually resumed in the 3060s through Robinson Standard BattleWorks and Kong Interstellar's rebuilt facilities, and a succession of increasingly advanced variants has kept the Black Knight relevant on the modern battlefield.
BMBlackKnight_BLXKNTDove.capabilities:
The Black Knight is an all-energy-weapon platform anchored by a Magna Hellstar II PPC, supported by two large lasers, four medium lasers, and a small laser integrated directly into its Beagle Active Probe. This sensor-weapon linkage allows the scanner to piggyback low-power laser pulses through interfering objects, providing detailed analysis of nearby targets that few other designs can match. Thirteen tons of Valiant Lamellor armor on a Technicron endo steel frame delivers exceptional survivability for a seventy-five-ton chassis, while the standard Vlar 300 engine provides a reliable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour without the fragility of an extralight powerplant.

The design's primary weakness has always been heat management. Despite mounting twenty single heat sinks, the sheer volume of energy weapons generates heat faster than the cooling system can dissipate it during sustained engagements. MechWarriors must exercise strict fire discipline, selecting weapon groups appropriate to the engagement range rather than attempting full alpha strikes. The original Black Knight's reputation in the Third Heavy Assault Regiment was that of a 'Mech which had to be literally dismembered to stop, and in one-on-one engagements between equally skilled pilots, conventional wisdom holds that the Black Knight will always triumph.
BMBlackKnight_BLXKNTDove.history:
The Black Knight debuted during the Reunification War in 2578 when Kong Interstellar Corporation's Third Heavy Assault Regiment (the Pythons) fielded the new design against the Taurian Concordat on Ridgebrook. Company commanders quickly discovered that the sophisticated electronics package made the Black Knight an outstanding command platform, and following its successful combat debut, the SLDF's First Corps and eventually the entire Defense Force adopted the design. By the height of the Star League, the Black Knight was a ubiquitous presence in SLDF formations, with Royal regiments fielding the advanced BL-6b-KNT variant equipped with double heat sinks and upgraded weaponry.

The collapse of the Star League and the devastation of the First Succession War proved catastrophic for Black Knight production. Kong Interstellar's orbital factories above Connaught were destroyed in 2802, and while the company managed to restart production in 2809 with the downgraded BL-7-KNT (replacing the endo steel chassis and advanced electronics with cruder but manufacturable alternatives) a Capellan Confederation raid permanently destroyed the line in 2820. Kong was reduced to producing spare parts and performing maintenance work, and the Black Knight's numbers slowly dwindled across the Inner Sphere as attrition and jury-rigged repairs took their toll.

During the Succession Wars, the remaining Black Knights were concentrated primarily in the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League, while the Capellan Confederation possessed none. ComStar maintained stockpiles of Star League-era machines, which proved invaluable when the Com Guards adopted the Black Knight as a command unit for Level II and Level III formations. Curiously, the handful of Black Knights provided to the Draconis Combine through Operation ROSEBUD was apparently the result of a clerical error. The Clans also maintained the design, though by the time of the Clan Invasion it had been relegated to solahma units.

The Battle of Tukayyid in 3052 marked the Black Knight's dramatic return to prominence. ComStar engineers developed the BL-9-KNT Clanbuster refit specifically for the engagement, equipping it with an XL engine, upgraded weapons, and a distinctive sword-like hatchet designed to exploit the Clans' disdain for physical combat. These machines proved remarkably effective in the close-quarters fighting of the Racice River Delta against Clan Smoke Jaguar and at Devil's Bath against the Steel Vipers, where the improved short-range firepower and melee capability caught Clan warriors off guard.

Robinson Standard BattleWorks secured a manufacturing license from Kong Interstellar in 3063, producing the technologically advanced BL-12-KNT with extended-range weapons and a targeting computer. Two years later, Kong itself rebuilt its Connaught plant and resumed Black Knight production. Through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, RSB released a succession of increasingly sophisticated BLK-NT variants incorporating Clan-specification weaponry, endo-composite structures, and advanced electronic warfare suites. When the Republic of the Sphere collapsed, Kong received the BLK-NT plans through a reciprocal licensing agreement with RSB and developed its own variant, the BL-18-KNT, updating the classic design with Clan weapons and a targeting computer. The Black Knight has thus endured across nearly six centuries of continuous service, proof of the fundamental soundness of Kong Interstellar's original design.
BMBlackKnight_BLXKNTDove.deployment: The original BL-6-KNT represents the Black Knight as Kong Interstellar intended it, a Star League-era heavy BattleMech built on an advanced Technicron endo steel chassis with a comprehensive energy weapons suite and integrated Beagle Active Probe. Introduced in 2578 for the SLDF, the design served as both a devastating front-line combatant and a sophisticated command platform. While production ceased during the Succession Wars, surviving examples remained prized possessions, and both Kong and Robinson Standard BattleWorks eventually returned the original configuration to production alongside newer variants.

BMMarauder_MADXRFalcon.overview: The Marauder was first designed by General Motors in 2612 as an attack and direct fire support BattleMech intended to usher in a new generation of heavy 'Mechs for the Star League Defense Force. Weighing seventy-five tons, the design quickly became one of the most recognizable and feared chassis on the battlefield, outclassed in raw power only by larger assault 'Mechs such as the Stalker and BattleMaster. During the Star League era, the Marauder's tremendous firepower and advanced electronics made it a favorite of the Gunslinger Program and endeared it to battalion and regimental commanders across the SLDF. When the Succession Wars shattered the technological base of the Inner Sphere, the Marauder endured as a devastating shock unit, with massed formations proving capable of breaking through even well-prepared defensive lines. Production spread across multiple manufacturers and nations, ensuring the design's survival through centuries of conflict, while repeated waves of technological recovery have kept the Marauder competitive well beyond what its original designers could have imagined.
BMMarauder_MADXRFalcon.capabilities:
The Marauder's armament centers on a pair of Magna Hellstar particle projector cannons mounted in armored gauntlets, supplemented by a dorsal-mounted General Motors Whirlwind autocannon. All three primary weapons share similar range profiles, allowing a skilled MechWarrior to concentrate devastating fire at long range. The arm pods utilize versatile ball-and-socket joints that provide superior traverse rates and fields of fire compared to more conventional mounting systems, while the durable construction of the Hellstar housings permits effective hand-to-hand combat when engagements close to point-blank range. A pair of Magna Mk II medium lasers in the arm pods provide additional close-range defense.

The Marauder's distinctive silhouette, once unique among BattleMechs, makes it a harder target than more humanoid designs. Eleven and a half tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provide solid protection, while a Vlar 300 fusion engine drives the seventy-five-ton chassis to a respectable cruising speed. However, the design is not without notable weaknesses. The autocannon's connection to the main chassis is tenuous and vulnerable to damage, while the waist rotation rings linking the upper body to the leg assemblies represent another structural concern. The powerful Dalban HiRez tracking system, positioned in the forward section, is also known to impede the pilot's direct field of view.
BMMarauder_MADXRFalcon.history:
The Marauder first entered service with the Star League Defense Force in 2612, where it rapidly gained a reputation as one of the premier heavy 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere. Royal SLDF brigades fielded the original MAD-1R with its ferro-fibrous armor and CASE-protected ammunition stores, later upgrading to the MAD-2R with extended-range particle cannons and double heat sinks by 2760. The design became synonymous with the Gunslinger Program, and its advanced electronics package made it a natural choice for senior officers commanding battalion and regimental formations.

The Succession Wars tested the Marauder's reputation and proved it well-deserved. As the Inner Sphere tore itself apart, the rarity of the design forced commanders to pair their Marauders with similar heavy 'Mechs such as the Warhammer and Thunderbolt to form effective strike lances. House Liao fielded only several hundred Marauders total by 2828, a scarcity reflected across every Great House. Each Successor State developed its own variant to address specific doctrinal needs and manufacturing constraints: House Davion introduced the MAD-3D in 2834, eliminating ammunition dependency by replacing the autocannon with a large laser; House Liao fielded the MAD-3L in 2905, swapping one PPC for a large laser to reduce heat; and the Free Worlds League produced the MAD-3M in 2873, replacing both PPCs with large lasers to leverage their domestic manufacturing strengths. Salvage culture during the late Third Succession War even spawned the MAD-3V, which incorporated components from destroyed Von Luckner tanks.

The recovery of the Helm Memory Core triggered a renaissance for the Marauder. House Davion rushed an upgraded variant into production, but their eagerness backfired when House Kurita captured Quentin and its Marauder factory during the War of 3039. The Federated Commonwealth responded with a second upgraded design, while Bowie Industries on Carlisle developed their own variant after the Draconis Combine captured plans for the Davion model. Multiple lostech-inspired variants reached the frontlines in time for the Clan Invasion, where the Marauder continued to prove its worth against technologically superior opponents.

A second revitalization came at the hands of the Capellan Confederation, which had never before produced the design. Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao personally negotiated the acquisition of manufacturing rights from General Motors on behalf of Ceres Metals Industries, resulting in the stealth-armored MAD-5L and later the plasma rifle-equipped MAD-6L. During the Jihad, Word of Blake-influenced designs complicated the Marauder's production arena, with Ibuki Robotics leveraging captured technology from Vicore Industries to produce the MAD-9W2, a design that proved popular across multiple militaries despite lingering Blakist stigma.

The Marauder's battlefield legacy spans centuries of engagements. During the Jade Falcon invasion of Trell I in 3050, Marauders of the Twelfth Donegal Guards engaged the elite Falcon Guards in desperate defensive actions through mountain passes, while on Yed Posterior in 3137, Republic militia employed a pair of MAD-7C Marauders with C3 and ECM capabilities to wage a devastating guerrilla campaign against Clan Wolf invaders. From the Star League's golden age through the fires of the Jihad and beyond, the Marauder has earned its place as one of the most enduring and respected BattleMech designs ever produced.
BMMarauder_MADXRFalcon.deployment: The definitive Succession Wars-era Marauder, this variant entered production in 2819 as a simplified version of the original design that could be manufactured with degraded industrial capacity. Stripped of the Royal variant's advanced features but retaining the proven weapons layout of twin PPCs, an autocannon/5, and paired medium lasers, the 3R became one of the most widely produced and recognized heavy BattleMechs in the Inner Sphere. Manufactured across multiple factories by General Motors, Bowie Industries, Independence Weaponry, and various Periphery producers, the 3R served with virtually every major military power and countless mercenary commands, cementing the Marauder's legendary reputation.
BMMarauder_MADXRFalcon.manufacturer: Bowie Industries|General Motors|Independence Weaponry|Pinard Protectorates Limited|Taurus Territorial Industries|Vandenberg Mechanized Industries

BMThunderbolt_TDRXSSparrow.overview:
The Thunderbolt was first produced in 2491 by Earthwerks Limited on Tikonov for the Capellan Confederation, representing the heaviest BattleMech the fledgling manufacturer could produce at the time. Designed from the outset as a planetary assault platform, the Thunderbolt, affectionately known as the T-Bolt or the Thud, established itself as one of the most formidable heavy ’Mechs of the Age of War. The design impressed the Confederation’s neighbors sufficiently that Earthwerks expanded into the Free Worlds League within fifteen years, establishing production on Keystone. Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten, Taurus Territorial Industries, and Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on Pinard further broadened the manufacturing base across the Inner Sphere and Periphery.

Renowned for its varied arsenal, exceptional armor protection, and an easily modified chassis, the Thunderbolt has remained in continuous production for over five centuries. Periodic updates have ensured the design remains competitive against newer heavy ’Mechs, and its ubiquity is such that virtually every military force in the Inner Sphere and Periphery fields at least one Thunderbolt in its ranks.
BMThunderbolt_TDRXSSparrow.capabilities:
The Thunderbolt’s greatest tactical asset is its eclectic weapons mix, which allows it to engage effectively at virtually any range. A Sunglow Type 2 large laser and Delta Dart LRM-15 launcher provide respectable long-range firepower, while three Diverse Optics Type 18 medium lasers mounted in a tight cluster and a Bical SRM-2 launcher deliver punishing close-range salvos. A pair of Voelkers 200 machine guns rounds out the arsenal for anti-infantry work. This combination enables the Thunderbolt to serve capably in roles ranging from fire support to brawling, a versatility few designs of its era can match.

Thirteen tons of Ryerson 150 armor provide protection that rivals or exceeds many assault ’Mechs, giving MechWarriors considerable confidence in sustained engagements. The Magna 260 fusion engine propels the chassis to a respectable sixty-four kilometers per hour, adequate for maintaining formation with most heavy lances. The Thunderbolt also features an exceptionally roomy cockpit compared to similarly sized designs, reducing pilot fatigue during prolonged campaigns.

The Thunderbolt’s well-known weakness is its inadequate heat dissipation. With only fifteen heat sinks struggling to manage the thermal output of its numerous energy weapons and missile systems, MechWarriors must carefully manage their rate of fire or risk shutdown and ammunition cook-off. Many commanders order their Thunderbolts into bodies of water at the outset of engagements, allowing pilots to fire their weapons more aggressively than the design’s cooling systems would otherwise permit.
BMThunderbolt_TDRXSSparrow.primaryFactory: Keystone, Sudeten, Tikonov, Taurus, Pinard, Braunschweig, Terra
BMThunderbolt_TDRXSSparrow.history:
The Thunderbolt’s origins trace to 2491, when Earthwerks Limited on Tikonov produced the primitive TDR-1C under the guidance of engineer Sarkia Menendez. Despite the Capellan Confederation’s relative inexperience with BattleMech technology, the design set records in development time and immediately proved its worth as a planetary assault platform. The upgraded TDR-5S entered production on Keystone within fifteen years, while Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten began manufacturing its own line. This broad production base established the Thunderbolt as a traditionally Capellan design that nonetheless became most closely associated with House Steiner and House Marik, the two largest producers during the Succession Wars.

The Succession Wars tested the Thunderbolt’s durability across centuries of grinding attrition. During the Second Succession War, Earthwerks on Tikonov attempted to preserve Star League technology through the TDR-5L, a downgraded Royal variant, but further industrial decline forced the creation of the even more simplified TDR-5LS by 2850. Both variants eventually vanished from production lines as the technology to build them was lost. Meanwhile, the standard TDR-5S continued to serve in virtually every major engagement, including the Battle of Chesterton in 2828 where Thunderbolts of the Seventh Tikonov Lancers clashed with Davion Crucis Lancers in brutal close-quarters fighting.

The Clan Invasion brought upheaval when Clan Jade Falcon conquered Sudeten, capturing Olivetti’s production lines. Though the Falcons continued producing Thunderbolts using what they considered outdated technology into 3054, the loss stung the Inner Sphere. Earthwerks responded with modernized variants, most notably the TDR-7M in 3049 and the ambitious TDR-9M in 3067. The latter sparked a legal confrontation with Irian BattleMechs Unlimited, which had introduced the Tempest as the Thunderbolt’s replacement. The Word of Blake brokered a compromise through a combat trial, which the TDR-9M won decisively, securing continued production and Blakist military contracts.

Trellshire Heavy Industries on Adelaide emerged as an important new manufacturer after barely surviving bankruptcy during the Clan Invasion. Initially producing retrotech garrison models during the Jihad, Trellshire gradually expanded to become the Lyran Commonwealth’s primary Thunderbolt supplier with the TDR-7S in 3091. Blackwell Industries also contributed the TDR-9W for Wolf’s Dragoons, drawing on a Golden Century-era Clan refit package. Earthwerks’ Tikonov facility continued production through multiple regime changes, including Republic of the Sphere control and the Capellan reconquest of 3145, where locally built Thunderbolts played decisive roles during Operation Golden Fortress and subsequent battles for the planet.

Nearing its seventh century on the battlefield, the Thunderbolt remains one of the most recognizable and widely produced BattleMechs in existence. Its durability and adaptability have ensured that no Inner Sphere or Periphery military is without at least one Thunderbolt in its inventory, whether obtained by purchase, license, or salvage.
BMThunderbolt_TDRXSSparrow.deployment: The definitive Thunderbolt variant, the TDR-5S has been in continuous production since approximately 2505 and remains the most widely recognized model of the chassis. Upgrading the primitive systems of the original TDR-1C to standard technology, the 5S established the template that nearly all subsequent variants would follow: a Sunglow Type 2 large laser, Delta Dart LRM-15, three Diverse Optics Type 18 medium lasers, a Bical SRM-2, and a pair of Voelkers 200 machine guns, all protected by thirteen tons of Ryerson 150 armor. Early production units reportedly struggled to achieve the designed top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, a shortcoming that Earthwerks’ marketing department attempted to obscure by falsely advertising a higher cruising speed. Manufactured across multiple worlds including Keystone, Sudeten, Taurus, and Pinard, the TDR-5S remains a staple of heavy lances throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery.
BMThunderbolt_TDRXSSparrow.manufacturer: Earthwerks-FWL Inc., Olivetti Weaponry, Earthwerks Ltd., Taurus Territorial Industries, Vandenberg Mechanized Industries, Lüneburg Vehicle Corporation, Earthwerks Incorporated

BMWarhammer_WHMXRMagpie.overview:
The Warhammer was introduced in 2515 by StarCorps Industries as a heavy fire-support platform capable of anchoring battle lines and devastating opponents at range. Designed in response to a procurement request for a mobile 'Mech with enough firepower to destroy or severely damage any 'Mech of the same weight class or lower, StarCorps delivered what would become one of the most iconic BattleMechs in history. The seventy-ton chassis quickly proved itself across every major conflict of the Star League era, earning a reputation as the backbone of heavy and battle regiments and a favorite mount of the legendary Star League Gunslingers.

Produced under license by manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and Periphery, the Warhammer's proliferation is rivaled by few designs. Its combination of devastating long-range firepower, respectable protection, and adaptable chassis has ensured a steady supply across all eras of warfare, with demand only increasing with each new conflict. Few BattleMech designs can claim as broad and continuous a production history as the Warhammer.
BMWarhammer_WHMXRMagpie.capabilities:
The Warhammer almost defines the heavy weight class of BattleMechs. Its rugged, stable chassis carries a pair of deadly arm-mounted particle projection cannons that give the design dependable firepower at range, capable of threatening even the heaviest armor. A six-tube Holly short-range missile system supplements these primary weapons and is itself backed by pairs of medium and small lasers and SperryBrowning machine guns, providing a layered defensive suite against infantry and light 'Mechs that close to exploit the PPC minimum range. This combination ensures the Warhammer remains dangerous at every engagement bracket.

With a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, the Warhammer can keep pace with most battle formations and its eighteen heat sinks allow it the freedom to move and fire without undue concern over heat buildup during sustained engagements. Respectable armor protection enables the design to absorb significant punishment while maintaining combat effectiveness, though the lack of jump capability limits its tactical flexibility in broken terrain. Dated but competitive electronics, including the O/P 3000 COMSET communications suite and O/P 1500 ARB targeting and tracking system, make the Warhammer equally capable of serving in the line of combat or in a command slot, a versatility that has kept it at the forefront of heavy lance doctrine for over five centuries.
BMWarhammer_WHMXRMagpie.history:
The Warhammer may be the best representation of the average citizen's view of the BattleMech. From the unwavering lines of the Star League Defense Force bringing down the Usurper, to the Periphery pirate screaming "Stand and Deliver," the Warhammer looms large over popular images of BattleMech warfare. First deployed in 2515, the design has served admirably in every major action in the Inner Sphere and beyond, from the liberation of Terra from Stefan Amaris to the bloody fields of Marduk in 3039. Every Successor State military makes use of the design, and it is held in high regard by mercenaries and Periphery nations alike.

Perhaps the most famous chapter in the Warhammer's long battlefield history occurred during the Marik Civil War in 3015, when Wolf's Dragoons fought their way through Duke Anton Marik's forces in engagements that became the stuff of legend. The fighting on Anton's New Delos saw Warhammers on both sides pushing their heat sinks to the limit in brutal close-quarters engagements that demonstrated the design's durability under extreme conditions. The Spirit Cat allies later witnessed the effectiveness of Marik Warhammers firsthand when the Regulan Hussars invaded Marik in 3147, where fire lances built around the design provided devastating covering fire for faster striker elements.

The Federated Commonwealth's Warhammer production capacity suffered a significant blow with the loss of the 'Mech's primary Olivetti factory on Sudeten to Clan Jade Falcon early in the Clan Invasion. The Commonwealth was reduced to refitting ancient Succession Wars machines to the -7S standard until Project Phoenix brought new Warhammers to the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth more than a decade later. Clan garrisons also developed various ClanTech refit kits for use on captured FedCom Warhammers, replacing the PPCs with pulse lasers on models not yet equipped with double heat sinks. The recovery of the Helm Core brought about a new generation of Warhammer variants, first in the form of refit kits and later with new production variants employing reclaimed technology, with extended-range cannons and improved heat-dissipating technology making an effective combination even against the Clan invaders.

The Free Worlds League found a booming business in the export of Warhammer refit kits in the years before and after the Clan Invasion, and the popularity of their kits and the deals made with other Houses during the conflict made Free Worlds League Warhammers ubiquitous throughout the Inner Sphere. Production of new units within the League was limited until early in the Jihad, when the Prince of Regulus backed a new Warhammer line on Wallis to supply BattleMechs for his ambitious plans. The Draconis Combine refit its own Warhammers to the -7K standard, and when a variant featuring paired heavy PPCs proved popular enough that other Houses began copying it, Alshain Weapons received funding to build a new Warhammer production line on Tok Do. With the renewed emphasis on tradition in the Draconis Combine, Alshain emphasized the classic chassis on all their Warhammers.

Wolf's Dragoons contracted to begin production runs on a Golden Century-era Clan Warhammer variant which was popular with the original Dragoons, fulfilling several Clans' subsequent requests for the model. The Taurian Concordat has constructed the Warhammer on Pinard since the 'Mech was first introduced, and after the discovery of the New Dallas Memory Core during the Jihad, SLDF Royal models were introduced into production. After the asteroid attack on Taurus, TTI CEO Matthias Commager won reconstruction bids that not only funded facility refurbishment but brought attention to a revitalized Taurus Territorial Industries, which chose the Warhammer as its new flagship product.
BMWarhammer_WHMXRMagpie.deployment: The original Warhammer configuration introduced in 2515, the 6R established the template that would define the chassis for centuries. Its combination of twin Donal PPCs, a Holly SRM-6 launcher, paired Martell medium and Magna small lasers, and twin Sperry Browning machine guns provided a versatile mix of long-range striking power and close-range self-defense. Eighteen single heat sinks proved adequate for sustained PPC fire, though MechWarriors learned to manage their volleys carefully during prolonged engagements. The integrated searchlight tied directly to the O/P 1500 ARB targeting system made the 6R a feared night fighter, a capability that saw frequent use during the Succession Wars. Produced across more than a dozen facilities throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery, the 6R remained in active production well into the thirty-first century, proof of the soundness of the original design.
